title: ArchAgent: Agentic AI-driven Computer Architecture Discovery

mechanism.domainTask: LLM-guided discovery of cache replacement policies in a ChampSim microarchitectural simulator
mechanism.populationDetail: An evolutionary database stores multiple evaluated policy programs and metadata for later sampling; the paper does not establish an ArchAgent-specific island or tree population.
mechanism.archiveDetail: The ranked evolutionary database preserves multiple high-performing prior policies for later reuse, but its capacity and exact survivor rule are not specified.
mechanism.replacementDetail: The paper says candidates are ranked and fed into an evolutionary database, but does not expose bounded capacity, eviction, migration, or MAP-Elites cell admission for the ArchAgent run.
mechanism.generationDetail: The LLM is asked to iteratively improve an existing ChampSim cache-policy code artifact, with sampled prior policies and metadata used as context; the paper does not expose a separate crossover operator.
mechanism.feedbackDetail: IPC speedup values, workload/configuration results, code-length measurements, simulator-validity outcomes, and prior-run metadata are reused in later prompts; no separate natural-language evaluator critique is exposed.
mechanism.parentSelectionDetail: Higher-ranked prior policies are preferred for reuse, while previous solutions and evaluator metadata are sampled into prompts; exact probability and parent cardinality are not reported.
mechanism.outOfTaxonomy: The paper combines an incompletely specified AlphaEvolve-style evolutionary database, simulator-backed hard-constraint gates, and a two-model ensemble whose call-level invocation protocol is not exposed.

provenance.sourcePdf: papers/ArchAgent Agentic AI-driven Computer Architecture Discovery.pdf
provenance.citationWarning: Do not infer island/MAP-Elites structure from the background discussion; database capacity/admission and true parent count are underspecified. The Gemini ensemble is clearly multi-model but routed-versus-collaborative behavior is unresolved. Placement under elitist replacement and static assignment is a cautious survey mapping rather than fully explicit paper evidence.
